newsitem.title: MEXICO: Lankenau confirms Confia purchase talks.
newsitem.headline: Lankenau confirms Confia purchase talks.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Abaco president Jorge Lankenau has confirmed that Citibank and Des Moines-based Principal International Group are considering buying stakes in its banking unit, Banca Confia.
"It's an issue that we are discussing ," Lankenau told a news conference late Wednesday.

The possible sale is part of an effort by Abaco to raise the remaining $165 million of a $250 million capitalization program at Confia. It pledged to muster that in exchange for offloading a chunk of past-due loans to the Bank Insurance Fund Fobaproa last year.
Financial authorities have said they want to see a healthy bank by June, but Lankenau denied there were time pressures.

The main headache was choosing the best option. Among the contenders are Citibank, Principal, and perhaps even General Motors, with which it has a partnership in an automobile credit plan and could provide a credit injection.
On the other hand, "it's very possible that this amount -- $165 million -- could in large part come from current shareholders," he said.
He left open the option of selling the entire institution.
"Obviously, there are other groups who want to buy complete control and if this is convenient to the institution and to the shareholders...Well, only my wife is not for sale," Lankenau said.

Confia has some 300 branches around Mexico and is considered a good retail outlet. Like all Mexican banks, it was side-swiped by Mexico's 1994-5 economic crisis, however. ((--Daniel Perez-Whitaker, Monterrey newsroom +528 435-7677))
